title: Games registry
description: data/games.json: every game the research draws from, its factions and expansions, and the rules that turn its numbers into our bands. Filled in for the whole starting scope before the research run, so all agents share one set of ids.

id.description: Short id used as the first part of unit ids. Expansions are never game ids.

kind.description: game = one title; series = researched as one entry through a representative title (e.g. Battlefield vehicle archetypes).

titles.description: For a series: the titles it covers.

control.description: commanded = the player orders units (RTS); piloted = the player is the unit (shooter); both.

research_bucket.description: The research batch this game belongs to: r1 Red Alert; r2 Tiberium series and Renegade; r3 Generals, Tempest Rising, Iron Harvest; r4 Company of Heroes, World in Conflict, Wargame, Broken Arrow; r5 Supreme Commander, Planetary Annihilation, StarCraft II, Halo Wars 2, Dawn of War; r6 shooters and hybrids (Battlefield, PlanetSide 2, Foxhole, WARDOGS, Arc Raiders, MechWarrior/BattleTech).

version_researched.description: Patch, edition or date the research describes.

factions.description: Playable sides. Use the reserved id 'shared' for units every side can field or games without factions. A unit belongs to the most general faction that fields it.

parent.description: For subfactions (e.g. a general or splinter group): the main faction id.

introduced_in.description: Expansion id, if the faction is not in the base game.

has_tiers.description: False if the game has no tech gating; its units then record no tier band.

has_costs.description: False if units are not bought; its units then record no cost band.

tier_map.description: Which tech gates map to which tier band.

gate.description: Building, research or level that unlocks units, in plain words.

faction.description: Faction id from this game's factions, e.g. 'soviet'.

cost_thresholds.description: Lowest price for each cost band above 'very low', in the game's currency. Method: pick an anchor, the price of the game's standard main battle tank (or its main line combat unit if it has no tanks); the thresholds are about 0.5, 0.9, 1.4 and 2 times the anchor, rounded. 'basis' names the anchor.

basis.description: The anchor unit and its price, and how a multi-resource cost is turned into one number.

speed_reference.description: The unit whose speed counts as 1.0 for speed bands, usually the basic rifle infantry.

damage_map.description: The game's own damage categories mapped to our damage types.

armour_map.description: The game's own armour categories mapped to our armour classes.

scope.description: starting = in the brief's list; added = added during research.

added_reason.description: Required for added games: the new mechanic it teaches.

teaches_patterns.description: For added games: the patterns that justified adding it.
